key_insight: A two-level machine-learning workflow can map free-energy stability across complex hybrid perovskite alloy spaces and show that stable compositions cluster at high iodine content.
engineering_relevance: The results narrow down composition targets for designing more stable solar-cell absorbers, especially by highlighting that Sn-based alloys have a smaller stable region than Pb-based ones.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials trained on DFT data handle efficient structure relaxations.
Secondary ML models predict energies directly from unrelaxed alloy structures.
The workflow evaluates free-energy landscapes across compositions, phases, disorder, and FA orientations.
evidence_signal: The approach enabled phase-stability calculations for quaternary (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3 alloys, revealing composition-dependent stability trends and no stabilization near the center of composition space.
watch_item: Because the stability maps rely on layered ML models and DFT training data, predictions may be sensitive to training coverage and transferability across underexplored alloy compositions.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
